spec.description: GreenLAG pipe lagging is an environmentally-friendly acoustic insulation system that combines a patented visco-elastic QuietWave noise barrier with acoustic foam for exceptional sound transmission loss, suitable for waste water pipes in residential, commercial, and industrial properties.
features: Acoustic foam for sound transmission loss
Soft microcellular material for vibration damping
Available in rolls, bends, strips, and junctions
No protective wear required for installation
install: Cut into strips to suit pipe size
Wrap around the pipe overlapping all joints by 50mm
Wrap three circumferential wraps of high quality 48-72mm wide reinforced aluminium tape at approximately every 350mm

NOTE :	THE NATIONAL OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY COMMISSION PRODUCED IN AUGUST 1988 A CODE OF PRACTICE AND GUIDANCE NOTES ON ASBESTOS.  IN THE PREFACE TO THAT DOCUMENT, PART 3, Clause 3.1, second paragraph states :
“ASBESTOS REMOVAL MAY NOT BE IMMEDIATELY NECESSARY, BUT MUST BE COMPLETED BEFORE A STRUCTURE OR PART OF A STRUCTURE IS DEMOLISHED.”
General
A.	Scope
The work of this section includes but is not limited to the following items:
Supply and installation of GreenLAG pipe lagging system.
A revolution in pipe lagging, GreenLAG is the superior solution for waste water acoustic insulation.
Combining a patented visco-elastic QuietWave noise barrier with acoustic foam, GreenLAG increases vibration damping through its soft microcellular material for exceptional sound transmission loss. Wrap it around waste water pipes or use it to minimise the noise break out of duct work, fan housings and valves in residential buildings, commercial and industrial properties.
The thinnest and lightest NCC-compliant acoustic pipe lagging available, GreenLAG is environmentally-friendly requiring no protective wear to install. It’s quick and easy to fit and can be supplied in rolls, bends, strips and junctions.
B.	Examine documents:  Examine parts of the drawings and this specification for requirements which affect the work of this specification.  In particular, take note of other trades involved.
C.	Co-ordination:  Co-ordinate with other trades affecting or affected by work of this section, co-operating as necessary to ensure steady and satisfactory progress of the work.
